🧳 External / portable drive · 🔊 Clicking or grinding noises

External Hard Drive Clicking, Grinding or Beeping

Clicking, grinding or beeping from the drive inside usually means the read/write heads or motor are failing. Each time you power it on, the damage can grow, and portable drives are easily hurt by drops.

5/5 · Pro territory
Success odds: Low

Mechanical faults worsen with every power-up, and real repairs need a cleanroom.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Unplug it and leave it off. Do not keep trying, because each power-up can scratch the platters.
  • Do not use the freezer trick, tap it, or shake it. These are myths that can do harm.
  • Never open the drive itself. Dust ruins the platters, and it needs a cleanroom.
  • Do not run recovery or repair software on a clicking drive. Heavy scanning stresses it.

Tools you'll use

GNU ddrescue

Copies a failing drive to an image file, retrying bad areas so you work from a copy, not the original.

  • Linux · macOS
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

HDDSuperClone

Linux tool for cloning a failing drive sector by sector, with options that skip and retry bad areas.

  • Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

ddrescueview

Free graphical viewer that shows which parts of a ddrescue image are good, bad or still unread.

  • Windows · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

smartmontools

Free open-source suite that reads S.M.A.R.T. health data from drives to show early signs of failure.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

TestDisk

Free open-source tool that finds lost partitions and repairs boot sectors so files can be read again.

🧑‍🔧 When to call a pro

If it clicks, grinds, beeps or will not spin and the data matters, stop and have a professional with a cleanroom look at it.

Questions people ask

Is clicking caused by the USB enclosure?

Usually no. The sound comes from the drive's moving parts. A weak power supply can trigger it on some portables, so trying a better power source once is reasonable.

Can I put it in the freezer?

No. It is a myth that can cause condensation damage. Experts advise against it.

Can I swap it into another enclosure?

It will not fix a mechanical fault, and some drives have soldered USB or encryption tied to the original board. Avoid it unless you know the model.
